_legal: Only intentionally public, government-published camera feeds. No private cameras, no auth bypass, no scanning.
_note: These URLs reference official government DOT infrastructure or open test infrastructure. URLs may change over time; replace with a working public HLS URL from your regional DOT or 511 system if any entry becomes unavailable.

demo_streams.name: Demo: HLS Test Stream (Mux Dev — always available)
demo_streams.notes: Public HLS test stream from Mux.com infrastructure. Always online. Not a real traffic camera — use this first to verify your pipeline and zone calibration work before connecting a real feed.

demo_streams.name: Iowa DOT — Cedar Rapids Traffic Camera (511ia.org)
demo_streams.notes: Official Iowa Department of Transportation traffic camera. Publicly accessible — part of the 511ia.org system. May be briefly offline during maintenance windows. If unavailable, try another iowadot.gov stream or use the Mux test stream.

demo_streams.name: Caltrans District 4 — Bay Area Freeway Camera
demo_streams.notes: Official California DOT (Caltrans) District 4 traffic camera on I-880 in the San Francisco Bay Area. Publicly embedded on quickmap.dot.ca.gov. HTTP (not HTTPS). Resolution typically 480p H.264. May occasionally return 403 on specific load-balancer nodes — if it fails, retry after a few seconds or switch to another source.

demo_streams.name: Custom URL (enter below)
demo_streams.notes: Enter any public HLS (.m3u8), MJPEG over HTTP, or RTSP stream URL you are authorized to access. Example sources: US state DOT / 511 systems, official city traffic portals, publicly published government streams.

_how_to_find_more_streams: 1. US State DOTs: Check 511<state>.gov or <state>dot.gov for live traffic camera pages. Open DevTools > Network > filter by .m3u8 to find the stream URL.
